hypothesis: If rrow-status.committed and rrow-dot for git-committed rows both use var(--green), the receipt rail conflates 'committed to git' with governance-ADMITTED (🟢), making it impossible to distinguish a version-control action from a ledger admission.
summary: index.html receipt rail renders COMMITTED rows (git commits 7703486, a5ab917) in --green (#3dd68c) via .rrow-status.committed (L256) and inline rrow-dot style (L948, L953). Source Atlas Doctrine assigns 🟢 exclusively to ADMITTED governance state. 'Committed to git' is an operational versioning action — it maps to 🔵 OBSERVED (#5b8af0) since the artifact is recorded in the VCS but has not passed the admission pipeline. Three distinct meanings share --green in index.html: (1) badge.live / mrow-dot.live / live-pulse = operational liveness [L91,123,133]; (2) rrow-status.committed / rrow-dot = git VCS commit [L256,948,953]; (3) station-verdict.go = governance GO verdict [L299]. The receipt rail (L940–960) is the highest-stakes site: an operator reading 'COMMITTED' in green naturally reads it as ledger-admitted — the identical color to the SA 🟢 glyph — when the actual state is only git-committed (pre-admission).
